title: Completed polynomial test rings and their lifting property
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $P=R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s,X_1,\ldots,X_d]$, where $s,d\geq0$, and let $e:P\twoheadrightarrow k$ be an $R$-algebra surjection with $e(X_i)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $\mathfrak q=\ker(e)$ and $S=\varprojlim_nP/\mathfrak q^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $S$ is Noetherian complete local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS$ and residue field canonically $k$. Each quotient $S/\mathfrak m_S^n$, $n\geq1$, is Artinian local with residue field $k$; therefore the same is true of $S/L$ whenever $\mathfrak m_S^n\subseteq L\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$. For $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], restriction along $P\to S$ gives a bijection between local $R$-maps $S\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ and $R$-maps $P\to A$ whose composite with $A\to k$ is $e$. For every surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ every such map $S\to A$ lifts to a local $R$-map $S\to B$ inducing the identity on $k$. Every local $R$-map from $S$ to a ring in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ is continuous for the maximal-ideal topology and factors through some $S/\mathfrak m_S^n$.

proof.text: Write $J=\mathfrak qS$ and $\iota:P\to S$ for the completion map. The polynomial ring $P$ is generated over $R$ by its $s+d$ variables, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Thus $\mathfrak q$ is finitely generated by the definition of Noetherianity. The map $e$ identifies $P/\mathfrak q$ with the field $k$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. This also covers $s+d=0$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 06SM constructs the completion at the kernel of a polynomial surjection to k.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with $A=M=P$ and $I=\mathfrak q$. It gives completeness and surjective projections $p_n:S\to P/\mathfrak q^n$ with kernel $\mathfrak q^nS$. Expanding products of generators gives $(\mathfrak qS)^n=\mathfrak q^nS$. Consequently these projections induce canonical ring isomorphisms $S/J^n\cong P/\mathfrak q^n$, compatible with $\iota$ and all quotient maps. (The module isomorphisms are ring isomorphisms because the projections preserve multiplication and one.) Thus $S$ is $J$-adically complete and separated, and $S/J\cong k$.

Here is the elementary unit calculation establishing locality, without assuming that $P$ is local. For $u\notin J$, choose $v\in S$ whose class in $S/J=k$ is the inverse of the class of $u$. Put $t=1-uv\in J$. In each $S/J^n$, the finite sum $1+t+\cdots+t^{n-1}$ is inverse to $1-t$; these sums are compatible as $n$ varies. Completeness from step 2 gives $w\in S$ with these coordinates, and separatedness gives $(1-t)w=1$. Hence $vw$ is inverse to $u$. Elements of $J$ cannot be units since $S/J$ is the nonzero field $k$. Thus the nonunits are precisely $J$, $S$ is local with maximal ideal $J$, and its residue map is $p_1$ followed by $P/\mathfrak q\cong k$.

source.place: Tag 06SM, lemma-exists-smooth, paragraph beginning "Let R be the m_P-adic completion of P"; explicit geometric-series verification using step 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] to the now Noetherian local ring $S$: for each $n\geq1$ and $J^n\subseteq L\subseteq J$, the ring $S/L$ is Artinian local with maximal ideal $J/L$. Its residue quotient is $(S/L)/(J/L)=S/J=k$. Taking $L=J^n$ proves the asserted special case, and the same application proves the assertion for every intervening ideal $L$.

For any Artinian local ring $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] gives $N\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$. Every local ring map $h:S\to A$ sends $J$ into $\mathfrak m_A$, and therefore kills $J^N$. It factors through $S/J^N$ and is continuous: the target maximal-ideal topology is discrete, and its kernel contains the open ideal $J^N$. This proves the last clause even without requiring the induced residue-field map to be the identity.

Fix $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ and its residue map $r_A:A\to k$. Given $f:P\to A$ with $r_Af=e$, one has $f(\mathfrak q)\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. Choose $N$ as in step 5. Then $f$ kills $\mathfrak q^N$; define $\widehat f:S\to A$ by $p_N:S\to P/\mathfrak q^N$ followed by the induced quotient map of $f$. This extends $f$, is an $R$-map, and its residue map is $p_1$ followed by $P/\mathfrak q\cong k$, so it is local and induces the identity on $k$. Conversely, a local residue-preserving $h:S\to A$ kills $J^N$ by step 5, so is determined by its map on $S/J^N$. Since $P\to S/J^N$ is surjective by step 2, it is determined by $h\iota$. Therefore restriction and the displayed extension are mutually inverse.

source.place: Tag 06SM (lemma-exists-smooth), final completion argument, specialized to polynomial P; explicit quotient construction using steps 2 and 5.

proof.text: Let $\pi:B\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjection in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ and $h:S\to A$ a local residue-preserving $R$-map. For each of the finitely many variables of $P$, choose in $B$ a preimage of its image under $h\iota$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives an $R$-map $g:P\to B$ with these chosen values and $\pi g=h\iota$. Because $\pi$ respects the specified residue maps, $r_Bg=r_A\pi g=e$. Apply step 6 with $B$ to extend $g$ to a local residue-preserving $\widehat g:S\to B$. The maps $\pi\widehat g$ and $h$ have the same restriction to $P$, hence are equal by the injectivity proved in step 6. No nilpotence of $\ker\pi$ is required for this variable-lifting argument. For no variables the unique structure map is used.

(2) adic-completion-noetherian(A=P,I=q) gives S Noetherian; module-completion-complete(A=M=P) gives completeness, ∩J^n=0, and p_n surjective with kernel q^nS=(qS)^n, so S/J^n≅P/q^n as rings. (4) noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local with K=L, hypotheses proved in steps 2-3. (5) m_A^N=0 makes local maps kill J^N; the discrete topology gives continuity. (6) f(q)⊆ker r_A=m_A, so f̂=f̄∘p_N; residue r_A f̂=ē∘p_1 makes it local; uniqueness from surjectivity of P→S/J^N. (7) Lift the variables via the universal property; r_B=r_A π; extend by step 6; equality by step-6 injectivity, with no small-extension assumption. Edge cases checked: s=d=0 (including R=k, q=0), n=1, L=J, A=k.
